issues.description: The algorithm is still quadratic (nested loops over j and i) and thus O(N^2) in time. With N up to 3×10^5 this will TLE / not finish within limits. The intended optimization (precomputing middle distinct counts incrementally) was not applied in a way that reduces the asymptotic complexity; the current code visits O(N^2) states and performs set operations per iteration.

The loops allow partitions where the middle subarray is empty (the case i == j-1 is processed: middle_set is empty for that iteration). The problem requires splitting into three non-empty contiguous subarrays. The current index/order of updates and loop bounds permit invalid splits and therefore can produce incorrect results. Additionally, the outer j loop begins at 1, which allows invalid small-j cases; the valid minimal j (given 1-based statement) must ensure a non-empty middle.
No automated tests were provided in the workspace (unit tests or sample-case tests). The repository lacks tests to validate correctness and to catch regressions or TLEs.

The design still relies on nested iteration over split positions. A scalable architecture would avoid O(N^2) by using linear-time techniques: e.g., two-pass scanning to compute prefix/suffix distinct counts combined with a linear sweep that maintains middle distinct counts (or using right-to-left accumulation of best-left + best-right values). The current module mixes index manipulation and set updates in a way that both permits invalid states and hinders a clear linear-time strategy.
